Source: https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1458

## Problem
`tests_update`, added in 2026.10.12 ("Edit linked-test metadata in place with preserved provenance"), writes new per-test fields: `metadata.tests[i].updated_by` and `metadata.tests[i].updated_at`. Hosts older than 2026.10.12 don't know these fields. When they canonicalize the item for hashing they drop them, so they compute a different item hash and report history corruption on a perfectly valid history.

In a fleet where agents use a newer global `pm` while the repository pins an older `@unbrained/pm-cli`, which is the normal state between Dependabot bumps, a single linked-test edit turns the repo's CI red.

## Real occurrence (public repo unbraind/pm-review, PR #1, pins 2026.10.10)
An agent ran `pm test <id> --update … --timeout 600` with a global 2026.10.13 host. History entry 23 of `pm-review-round`:
```json
{"op":"tests_update","patch":[
 {"op":"add","path":"/metadata/tests/0/timeout_seconds","value":600},
 {"op":"add","path":"/metadata/tests/0/updated_by","value":"codex-agent"},
 {"op":"add","path":"/metadata/tests/0/updated_at","value":"2026-10-13T12:56:35.894Z"},
 {"op":"replace","path":"/metadata/updated_at","value":"2026-10-13T12:56:35.894Z"}]}
```
Same files, two hosts:
```text
pm 2026.10.13 history pm-review-round --verify  → ok:true, current_matches_latest:true
pm 2026.10.10 history pm-review-round --verify  → ok:false
  errors: verify_failed:after_hash_mismatch:entry_23, verify_failed:current_item_hash_mismatch
```
CI (pinned 2026.10.10) then fails `pm health` with `history_drift_chain_mismatch:pm-review-round` and `history_drift_hash_mismatch:pm-review-round`.

A second agent in another repo (pm-context) hit the same thing. The pinned host also *rewrote* the tests block and dropped `updated_by`/`updated_at` when it next touched the item, so the "fix" an agent reaches for is data loss: re-anchoring history with the older host.

## Why this matters
The CLI's core promise is that many agents on many branches can work on one tracker and merge losslessly. Mixed host versions are unavoidable in that world: global installs, pinned devDependencies and CI images all drift. This is the same class as #976, #1040 and #1162, now triggered by a new feature's fields rather than by hashing changes.

## Proposal
1. **Forward-compatible hashing:** older hosts hash unknown nested fields verbatim instead of dropping them, or the canonical form is declared field-agnostic for `metadata.tests[]` entries.
2. **Or gate new fields behind a declared format/feature version:** a newer host writing to a tracker whose `settings.json` / format_version predates the feature either refuses or writes the legacy shape, unless the tracker opts in (for example `pm workspace upgrade`).
3. **Diagnostics:** when verification fails on an op the verifying host doesn't recognize, or on fields it doesn't know, report `history_written_by_newer_host` (naming the op and fields) rather than generic chain/hash drift, and recommend upgrading the verifying host. Never suggest a re-anchor that drops the newer data.
4. A cross-version test matrix: history written by N verifies under N-1 and N-2 for every new op and field.


Intake scope

Investigate reports that 2026.10.12+ tests_update editor stamps are dropped by older published hosts sharing item_hash_version3, causing false corruption and subsequent nested-field loss. Expand real published-artifact compatibility beyond top-level extension fields and retain original append-only evidence.

Duplicate check: complete live2953-item all-status corpus plus search/open/in-progress reads. Full closed pm-9djr6d implements linked-test editing with provenance; full closed pm-pae3wo implements real two-prior-release matrix for unknown top-level extension fields. Current matrix source tests top-level fields but does not exercise tests_update nested stamps. No existing open owner for this specific reported regression was found. Issue1458 and all paginated comments including independent pm-github occurrence6149865337 read. Treat external reproduction as reported evidence until independently reproduced; retain shipped predecessors and relate them rather than reopening unrelated completed scopes.
GH-1458: Preserve linked-test edit history across older published readers and writers

Investigate reports that 2026.10.12+ tests_update editor stamps are dropped by older published hosts sharing item_hash_version3, causing false corruption and subsequent nested-field loss. Expand real published-artifact compatibility beyond top-level extension fields and retain original append-only evidence.

Reproduce nested linked-test editor stamps through actual 2026.10.9/10/13 artifacts in isolated trackers; Verify exact nested values, before/after commitments, ordinary mutation, restore and native merge; New writers refuse unsupported format writes or preserve declared cross-version hash semantics; Diagnostics recommend a supported verifier upgrade and never destructive history re-anchoring; Compatibility coverage executes every newly written operation and nested field against supported prior hosts
